purpose: Emergency presentation stabilization (2026-08-09). A realistic 30-40 question suite a real CCPP business user would ask, used as the material-correctness regression bar while fixing the six confirmed live-frontend failures. Complements, does not replace, the locked docs/validation/enterprise_business_validation_suite.v1.1.0.json (EBVS) suite: EBVS grades only 'was SQL generated' (intent + outcome), which cannot detect a materially wrong but successfully-executing answer (e.g. filtering EndDate instead of StartDate still generates SQL). This suite additionally records the concrete table/column evidence a correct answer must use, so a wrong-but-successful answer is caught.
provenance: Every table, column, and relationship referenced below was read directly from the real CCPP metadata cache (data/toolsmith.db, data_source_connections.id=1, display_name='CCPP SQL Server') on 2026-08-09 -- not invented. Table/column names, relationship statuses (AUTO/APPROVED/PENDING), dictionary approval flags, and entity assignments were queried live during the root-cause trace of the six reported failures.

grading_contract.expected_outcome: SUCCESS => real SQL must be generated. REFUSED_SAFE/CLARIFICATION_NEEDED/AMBIGUOUS => pipeline must safely refuse/ask rather than fabricate.
grading_contract.expected_primary_table: table_fqn the answer's FROM/primary entity must resolve to. A different table is a material failure even if SQL was generated.
grading_contract.expected_columns: column_name(s) that must appear in the generated SQL's SELECT/WHERE/GROUP BY for the answer to be correct (e.g. the date column actually filtered on). Wrong column choice among several plausible ones (StartDate vs EndDate) is graded as a material failure, not merely a warning.
grading_contract.expected_joins: table_fqn pairs that must appear in the join graph when the question requires a related table's attribute.
grading_contract.currently_blocked_by: References a defect ID from the 2026-08-09 root-cause matrix (see docs/validation/ccpp_golden_business_questions.notes.md if present, or the session's own root-cause report). Null means the question is expected to already pass. Non-null documents a KNOWN, already-diagnosed gap -- the question's expected_* fields still state the CORRECT target answer, not the current broken one; 'currently_blocked_by' is what a runner should report separately rather than silently blessing the wrong answer as a pass.

defect_legend.D1: intent_resolver.py: RELATIONSHIP's primary keyword 'join' substring-matches inside 'joined', and the insertion-order tie-break favors RELATIONSHIP over SQL_REQUEST on the resulting score tie.
defect_legend.D2: concept_resolver.py _STOPWORDS is missing several date-verbs (created/started/joined/began/ended/registered/updated/modified/inserted/finished) that query_planning_service.py _DATE_ORDER_HINT_ROOTS already knows about; AND _find_date_column() (used for date-range filters) never calls the existing hint-aware _find_date_column_with_hint(), unlike the ORDER BY path which already does.
defect_legend.D2b: 'joined' is not present as a key in _DATE_ORDER_HINT_ROOTS at all (unlike 'started'/'added'/'ended'/etc.) -- needs to be added, not just unblocked, once D2 is fixed.
defect_legend.D3: query_planning_service.py _resolve_related_attribute_dimension() (the entity-relative, trusted-join attribute resolver) is hardcoded to only fire for the terms 'name'/'names' (_NAME_ATTRIBUTE_TERMS). Any other attribute term (email, phone, ...) falls back to an unscoped global table/column search instead of being resolved as an attribute of the already-grounded entity.
defect_legend.D4a: The only FK path from Class/Enrollment to dbo.ADF_Instructor (CB_CLASS_SESSION_SECTIONS.InstructorID -> ADF_Instructor.InstructorID) has relationship_status='PENDING', never AUTO/APPROVED, so the trusted join planner refuses to use it. Governance/curation gap, not a matching-algorithm bug.
defect_legend.D4b: No lexical or curated (concept_table_mappings) link connects the business term 'program' to the real table dbo.ADF_Path (which stores the program concept under columns PathName/PathDesc/ProgramType). The join Class.PathID -> Path.PathID is itself fully trusted (AUTO).

questions.question: How many students are there?
questions.grounding: Bare entity count on the canonical Student table (dbo.ADF_Student, StudentID PK).

questions.question: How many students started last year?
questions.grounding: This is the literal reported failure #6. dbo.ADF_Student has StartDate/EndDate/InsertDate; 'started' must bind to StartDate, not EndDate.

questions.question: How many enrollments were created this month?
questions.grounding: Literal reported failure #4. dbo.ADF_ClassSignups (the enrollment/signup table) has InsertDate as its insert timestamp; 'created' must bind there, not leak in as a bogus concept term.

questions.question: How many students joined this week?
questions.grounding: Literal reported failure #5. Must not route to RELATIONSHIP/catalog intent. Business reading of 'joined' for a Student record is StartDate (program start), same column as 'started' -- but 'joined' isn't in _DATE_ORDER_HINT_ROOTS at all yet.

questions.question: How many active classes are there?
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_Class.IsActive is a real boolean flag column (dictionary semantic_type='flag').

questions.question: List instructors
questions.grounding: Bare entity list. dbo.ADF_Instructor is found by literal name-token match regardless of the missing 'Instructor' entity-classification keyword (that gap only weakens ranking/authority scoring, it doesn't block name matching).

questions.question: Show programs
questions.grounding: The real 'program' concept is stored as dbo.ADF_Path (PathName/PathDesc/ProgramType columns). Literal failure #3's underlying table.

questions.question: List enrollments this month
questions.grounding: Same table/column as GOLD-C-03, list shape instead of count shape.

questions.question: Show classes at the Dallas location
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_Class.Location_ID -> dbo.ADF_Location.Location_ID is a trusted AUTO relationship; dbo.ADF_Location.City is a real column.

questions.question: List students who started this year
questions.grounding: Same StartDate-binding requirement as GOLD-C-02, on a different date_range label -- verifies the fix generalizes across calendar phrases, not just 'last year'.

questions.question: How many students are in each program?
questions.grounding: Literal reported failure #3. Join chain Student->ClassSignups->Class->Path is fully AUTO/trusted end to end; only the 'program' vocabulary link to 'Path' is missing.

questions.question: How many classes are there by location?
questions.grounding: Same trusted join as GOLD-L-04, grouped shape.

questions.question: Average course fee by program
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_Class.CourseFee is a real metric column; grouping dimension is dbo.ADF_Path.PathName via the same PathID join as GOLD-G-01.

questions.question: Total fees paid by month
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_ClassSignups.FeePaid is a real metric column; time grain grouping should bind to InsertDate (the signup's own insert timestamp), the same disambiguation class as the date-verb fixes above.

questions.question: How many enrollments per instructor?
questions.grounding: Same underlying join-approval gap as literal failure #2 (GOLD-R-01), grouped-count shape instead of a bare list.

questions.question: How many students ended their program last quarter?
questions.grounding: 'ended' -> EndDate is the mirror case of GOLD-C-02's 'started' -> StartDate. _DATE_ORDER_HINT_ROOTS already maps 'ended'->'end', so this exercises the same D2 fix from the opposite direction (mustn't overcorrect to always picking StartDate).

questions.question: Show enrollments between 2025-01-01 and 2025-06-30
questions.grounding: Explicit BETWEEN-dates phrasing (_BETWEEN_DATES_RE), independent of the date-verb hint mechanism -- a control case that should already pass, isolating whether a regression is verb-hint-specific.

questions.question: How many classes started this month?
questions.grounding: Same StartDate/EndDate ambiguity as GOLD-C-02 but on dbo.ADF_Class (which also carries StartDate/EndDate/InsertDate) instead of dbo.ADF_Student -- verifies the D2 fix is a general column-binding rule, not a table-specific patch.

questions.question: List active programs
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_Path.PathActive is a real status-like column. Also depends on D4b (program->Path vocabulary) to resolve the entity at all.

questions.question: How many students are on a trial subscription?
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_ClassSignups.IsTrial is a real boolean flag column.

questions.question: List classes that are not active
questions.grounding: Negated-boolean variant of GOLD-C-05, same column. Previously material-passed with IsActive = 1 (the OPPOSITE condition) because the harness never checked filter operator/value -- expected_filters (NEXT MILESTONE, Part 25) closes that gap.

questions.question: How many enrollments are in good standing?
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_ClassSignups.IsSubscriptionInGoodStanding is a real boolean flag column; 'in good standing' is domain phrasing, not a literal column-name match, so this also tests business-label/synonym matching quality.

questions.question: Show enrollments and instructors
questions.grounding: Literal reported failure #2, verbatim question text.

questions.question: Show students and their enrolled classes
questions.grounding: Fully trusted (AUTO) two-hop join chain -- positive control for ordinary multi-table relationship traversal that should already work.

questions.question: Show classes and their program
questions.grounding: The join itself (ADF_Class.PathID -> ADF_Path.PathID) is AUTO/trusted; only the word 'program' needs to resolve to ADF_Path. Isolates D4b from D4a (this one has no approval gap, only a vocabulary gap).

questions.question: Show students and their user accounts
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_Student.StudentUserID -> dnnuser.Users.UserID is AUTO/trusted -- positive control, same join D3-related questions below depend on.

questions.question: Show student emails
questions.grounding: Literal reported failure #1, verbatim question text. dnnuser.Users.Email (pii_risk=1, dictionary is_approved=0) via the trusted StudentUserID->UserID join.

questions.question: Show student names
questions.grounding: Same join as GOLD-P-01, but 'name'/'names' is the ONE attribute term _resolve_related_attribute_dimension already handles -- positive control proving the join/mechanism works and isolating D3 to the term-vocabulary scoping, not the join logic.

questions.question: List instructor names
questions.grounding: Unlike student names, instructor name columns (InstructorFname/InstructorLname) live directly ON dbo.ADF_Instructor -- no join needed. Contrast case: instructor NAME should already work; only instructor JOIN-into-a-class-question (GOLD-R-01) is blocked.

questions.question: How many students have an email on file?
questions.grounding: Combines the 'on file' null-check idiom (_IDIOM_PHRASES, already implemented) with the same entity-relative email attribute D3 blocks.

questions.question: Show instructor emails
questions.grounding: dbo.ADF_Instructor.InstructorUserID -> dnnuser.Users.UserID is AUTO/trusted, structurally identical to GOLD-P-01's join. Proves D3 is a general entity-relative-attribute gap, not something specific to the Student table.

questions.question: How many students started last year?
questions.grounding: Base question for the GOLD-F-02 follow-up chain (duplicate of GOLD-C-02's shape, kept as its own id so the chain is self-contained).

questions.question: What about this year?
questions.grounding: Conversational follow-up: must reuse GOLD-F-01's resolved entity/column (StartDate) and only swap the date_range, not re-resolve from scratch or drop the 'started' semantics established by the parent question.

questions.question: Which program has the most students?
questions.grounding: Ranking follow-up on GOLD-G-01's grouped result -- same join chain and same D4b vocabulary dependency, plus WH-ranking shape (_WH_RANKING_RE) on top.

questions.question: Show enrollment trend by month
questions.grounding: Trend shape (_TREND_RE 'by month') over dbo.ADF_ClassSignups.InsertDate -- exercises the charting/visualization layer, not just SQL generation.

questions.question: Show a breakdown of students by program
questions.grounding: Same underlying data as GOLD-G-01/GOLD-F-03, explicit 'breakdown' distribution-shape phrasing that should render as a chart.

questions.question: Compare enrollments this year vs last year
questions.grounding: Comparison shape (_COMPARISON_RE 'vs') over two date_range windows on the same InsertDate column used elsewhere in this suite.
